captions.threads:
Doubt keeps showing up right after I say yes. Ink barely dry, and my brain is already pulling out old decisions and holding them up to the light. Day four is its favorite day.

I used to read that as proof I messed up. Less sure now. Sometimes doubt is fear in a costume. Sometimes it's the first honest thing I've heard about what I want. The trick is figuring out which one is talking.

The question I keep coming back to: is it about the work, or about being seen doing the work? Those feel identical at 2am. They aren't. If it's the work, the path might need adjusting. If it's being seen, I probably stay put and let the discomfort do its thing.

entries.postTitle: The Overstimulation Trap: Why Busy Input Makes Your Output Disappear

captions.threads:
so i sit down to create and i have exactly 40 minutes. the perfect window. except nothing happens. brain's just static. and i spent the last three hours scrolling, listening to podcasts, checking messages, doom-scrolling news. my nervous system is already maxed out before i even opened the blank page.

turns out your creative bandwidth isn't separate from your input diet. you can't be feeding your attention raw stimulus all day and then wonder why the well's dry when you need to actually make something. it's not laziness or lack of ideas. it's overstimulation masquerading as nothing-to-say.

the weird part? pulling back on input doesn't feel like relief at first. feels boring. quiet. wrong even. but that's actually your system downregulating. that's the reset happening.

if you're hitting this wall, the output problem isn't output. it's what you let in all morning.
